items.title: Closed runtime-mode and overlay canon is explicit
items.statement: Run_Modes owns a closed four-value runtime enum, keeps workflow overlays separate, forbids overlay-based authority widening, and requires children to inherit or narrow the parent ceiling.
items.impact: Builders and consumers have one deterministic authority vocabulary instead of inventing extra modes.

evidence.exact_quote: The closed runtime-mode enum is `ask|plan|regular|yolo`; the closed workflow-overlay enum is `none|plan|deep_plan|debug|interview|brainstorm|crew`.
children inherit the parent runtime ceiling and may narrow it only.

items.title: HTE keeps every real action host-owned
items.statement: HTE separates provider reasoning from action authority: PM executes every tool call through permissions and FileSafe, and provider-originated tool use is terminally forbidden.
items.impact: This is a strong authority boundary and a directly testable provider-adapter invariant.

evidence.exact_quote: HTE is a **host-owned action loop**: the provider may request the next hosted action or return a final answer, but Puppet Master executes every real tool call itself under the permission + FileSafe stack and feeds the structured result back into the next provider turn.

items.title: DAE isolates canonical workspace writes
items.statement: DAE must execute in a PM-managed jail, treat actual jail diff as mutation truth, keep the canonical workspace non-writable, and reconcile only after scans and FileSafe checks.
items.impact: The core delegated-execution containment model is explicit and not left to adapter discretion.

evidence.exact_quote: The canonical workspace MUST NOT be directly writable during DAE. Host-side reconciliation applies the verified jail diff back only after scans and FileSafe checks succeed.
The **actual jail diff** is authoritative for mutation accounting; provider-reported tool/file activity is advisory correlation data only.

items.title: Concurrent child-jail reconciliation has no merge transaction
items.statement: Each DAE child receives its own jail, but this owner text does not define reconciliation ordering, conflict detection, atomic application, stale-base rejection, or rollback when sibling diffs touch the same canonical path.
items.impact: Parallel children can pass isolated scans yet race or overwrite one another during host reconciliation.

evidence.exact_quote: Workspace isolation is per-subagent: HTE child/subagent turns inherit the parent write-scope because PM executes tools, while DAE child/subagent turns run in their own jail and reconcile back only after scans and FileSafe checks succeed.

items.title: Per-account DAE eligibility and account-switch ordering are explicitly unresolved
items.statement: The selection algorithm is deterministic only for its declared snapshot; the document itself records that per-account DAE eligibility and child account re-resolution ordering are missing, and that mid-run account switches can invalidate committed strategy.
items.impact: A run can select DAE under one identity and continue under another identity whose provider/account policy does not authorize DAE.

evidence.exact_quote: strategy selection remains blind to per-account DAE eligibility and child-run account re-resolution ordering.
mid-run account-switch invalidation of committed strategy

items.title: Concurrency queue ordering and recovery are unspecified
items.statement: The caps and queue-on-full behavior are exact, but no fairness key, priority policy, cancellation semantics, durable queue identity, or crash/pause replay ordering is defined.
items.impact: A conforming implementation can still starve work, reorder queued children nondeterministically, or duplicate admission after recovery.

evidence.exact_quote: Queueing at concurrency caps is deterministic; PM MUST NOT silently discard or auto-widen queued work.

items.title: Run-envelope budget inheritance is bounded
items.statement: Budgets are frozen for a run, survive pause/resume, distinguish nesting from tool rounds, and allow per-run or child narrowing without widening the policy ceiling.
items.impact: Budget propagation has a clear monotonic ceiling.

evidence.exact_quote: Budget overrides MAY narrow defaults per run, but MUST NOT widen beyond the hard policy ceiling.

items.title: Pre-dispatch kill reasons and terminal outcomes are deliberately separated
items.statement: The consumer contract distinguishes kill.* supervisor triggers from done.* terminal reasons, retires kill.task_timeout as a consumer alias, and keeps pre-request and post-response budget exhaustion distinct.
items.impact: Persisted event consumers can avoid collapsing materially different budget and timeout phases.

evidence.exact_quote: Run outcome naming follows a two-family reason-code contract: `kill.*` names pre-dispatch or `/active-kill` supervisor triggers, while `done.*` names terminal outcomes recorded after shutdown, usage, or recovery finalization.

`kill.budget_exceeded` remains pre-dispatch only. Post-response budget-overrun cases use terminal `done.budget_exceeded` after usage has been durably recorded and MUST NOT be folded back into the pre-dispatch row above.

items.title: Process-group shutdown and crash recovery are strongly specified
items.statement: The plan owns a single signal fan-out, isolated process groups, platform-specific grace periods, idempotent shutdown, durable event flushing, and crash-marked startup recovery.
items.impact: Subprocess leaks and silent loss of unfinished runs are explicit non-gaps.

evidence.exact_quote: `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` request graceful shutdown. `SIGHUP` triggers config reload, not shutdown. Every managed provider, MCP, terminal, and LSP subprocess MUST run in its own process group (`setsid` on Unix; `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` on Windows) so signal delivery stays scoped to the `/process-group` rather than individual PIDs.
PM MUST NOT silently drop an incomplete run or rewrite it as `done.failed` without the crash marker

items.title: Shutdown outcome precedence is not total
items.statement: Durability-flush failure escalates to done.crashed, while user or parent cancellation remains done.cancelled even after forced termination; the simultaneous case has no stated precedence or multi-reason encoding.
items.impact: Two implementations can persist different coarse outcomes for the same cancelled run whose final flush fails.

evidence.exact_quote: if durability flush fails, PM emits a structured diagnostic and the terminal outcome escalates to `done.crashed` rather than claiming a clean shutdown
user-driven or parent-driven cancellation produces `done.cancelled`, not `done.failed`, even if force termination is needed after the grace window

items.title: Helper health monitoring has no measurable restart oracle
items.statement: Memory-pressure monitoring and controlled restart are mandatory, but threshold units, sampling window, sustained-growth definition, hysteresis, restart budget, and unhealthy-helper routing are not specified here.
items.impact: The requirement cannot be implemented or falsified consistently, and oscillating restarts can amplify outages.

evidence.exact_quote: sustained growth beyond configured restart thresholds emits `diagnostic(category="resource_pressure")` or equivalent structured telemetry

items.title: Shell-failure and write-thrash counting exclude false positives
items.statement: The plan precisely defines executed-shell fingerprints, reset behavior, normalized file identity, qualifying mutations, sliding-window timing, and exclusions for denied, blocked, UI-only, no-diff, rollback, and PM-owned operations.
items.impact: Policy denials and UI operations cannot accidentally consume runtime kill budgets.

evidence.exact_quote: permission denials, FileSafe blocks, validation failures, missing execution due to policy, and synthesized reconciler closures do **not** count as shell failures
denied, blocked, no-diff, rollback, and Puppet-Master-owned post-processing writes do **not** count

items.title: Mandatory DAE scans lack a finalization transaction boundary
items.statement: All three scans are required before finalization, but their ordering, timeout/retry policy, snapshot identity, mutation freeze, and atomic relationship to reconciliation and terminal-event persistence are not defined.
items.impact: The workspace can change between scan and apply, or a crash can persist a terminal outcome without a provably matching scanned diff.

evidence.exact_quote: When a DAE run completes (any terminal outcome), the following scans MUST execute before the outcome is finalized:
Scan failures escalate the outcome to `done.failed` with reason `kill.post_scan_failure`.

items.title: Coarse outcome taxonomy is closed and persisted

items.impact: Consumers have a stable terminal-state model and identity rule.

evidence.exact_quote: Every run terminates with exactly one canonical coarse outcome value.
normalized `done.payload.status` remains a coarse transport-facing status (`success | cancelled | failed`), while `done.payload.outcome` carries the canonical taxonomy above

items.impact: Secrets or private data can persist in jail storage, diffs, logs, or crash artifacts beyond the run without a canonical deletion or audit rule.

evidence.exact_quote: DAE uses an **ephemeral Puppet Master-managed jail** (prefer a dedicated worktree; otherwise an equivalent isolated workspace) and the provider sees only jail paths.
DAE-jail durability across pause/resume
